title: New Orleans funerals as a gimmick
summary: Dance and Caldwell say the New Orleans funeral band has become a gimmick, and that street funerals have faded in New York.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: You know, the thing that strikes me as funny, when you come to think of it, is all that business of the New Orleans funerals, marching out and playing, the band playing back. Now, you know, they've made a sort of a gimmick of that really.
I don't -- in a way that's a kind of mockery.
It is, true. We was [crossed out] there.

"Didn't he they do Ramble." They It's kind of a mockery because it's -- used to play that thing coming back from the funeral-- the "Free as the cemetery, (unintelligible) birds", like that, you know, because we used to -- years ago in New York, had like the big person was -- had died, like Mason or Odd- fellows. They don't have those funerals up and down the streets anymore in New York like they did years ago. They don't have them anymore. Mostly they do the thing at the temple or at the big funeral parlor. Even whites don't have that much like they used to.
